figures.title: Complex structure and interface overview
figures.question: Do the variants differ in complex geometry, internal deformation, or interface contacts?
figures.reading: Each dot is one replicate mean. Bars show the system mean ± between-replicate SD. RMSDs use a common WT backbone reference; the panel titles distinguish CH3 alignment from self-fitting.
figures.interpretation: System means for complex size and partner separation are similar, while domain/receptor RMSDs and local interactions vary.
figures.limitation: SD bars are not confidence intervals. Similar global dimensions do not establish equivalent structures or interfaces.

figures.title: Whole-partner MM/GBSA comparison
figures.question: Which variants have a reproducible shift in the calculated binding-associated energy?
figures.reading: Left: replicate means with between-replicate SD. Right: variant minus WT with unadjusted 95% Welch intervals. Positive differences are less favorable within this model.
figures.interpretation: D265A has the clearest unfavorable shift (+10.02 kcal/mol); its Holm-adjusted p-value is 0.0645. All other unadjusted intervals cross zero.
figures.limitation: These are whole-partner MM/GBSA estimates without entropy, not measured affinities or interface-only energies.

figures.title: Electrostatic compensation and other components
figures.question: Which calculated components account for the mean differences from WT?
figures.reading: The left panel separates direct electrostatics (EEL) and GB solvation (EGB). The right panel shows their sum beside van der Waals and surface contributions. Positive values are unfavorable differences.
figures.interpretation: For D265A, approximately +148.4 kcal/mol in EEL is offset by −141.0 kcal/mol in EGB, leaving +7.39 kcal/mol net polar.
figures.limitation: Bars are descriptive means without uncertainty intervals. They do not assign energies to particular interface residue pairs.

figures.title: Contact counts versus whole-partner energy
figures.question: Do replicate-level contact counts covary with the calculated energy?
figures.reading: Each point is a replicate; colors identify systems. The two panels use total heavy-atom contact pairs and salt-bridge candidate pairs.
figures.interpretation: Use this as an exploratory comparison of structural and energetic variation, rather than fitting a mechanism from the pooled points.
figures.limitation: Between-system and within-system variation are mixed; contact counts do not measure interaction strength.

figures.title: Heavy-atom contact changes — page 1 of 4
figures.question: Which protein and glycan residue pairs gain or lose sampled contact occupancy?
figures.reading: Rows identify original chain/residue labels; columns are variants. Red means more frequent contact than WT; blue means less frequent. Values are percentage-point changes, with a fixed ±100 scale. Only pairs reaching 20% mean occupancy in any system are displayed.
figures.interpretation: Pages continue the same list, ordered by largest absolute primary change. Page 1 includes the large A327S change in the Fc A N297 glycan residue 2–receptor N162 NAG contact.
figures.limitation: A: and B: are Fc chains; C: is receptor. Glycan numbers label individual rings, not the whole glycan. These primary heatmaps use 4.5 Å and 50 ps sampling; use the sensitivity figures to judge dependence on those choices.

figures.title: Salt-bridge candidate occupancy changes
figures.question: Which charged interface residue pairs change their geometric salt-bridge occupancy?
figures.reading: Colors show variant minus WT occupancy. A:265–C:120 is Fc chain A Asp265–receptor Lys120; B:265–C:161 is Fc chain B Asp265–receptor Lys161.
figures.interpretation: The chain A Asp265–Lys120 candidate occurs in 97.4% of primary WT samples and is absent in D265A.
figures.limitation: Loss after removing Asp charge is an expected chemical consequence, not an independent estimate of its energetic contribution. The criterion is distance-based and assumes fixed protonation.

figures.title: Fc CH3 backbone RMSD — individual trajectories
figures.question: Are there trends, shifts, or persistent differences among replicates?
figures.reading: Residual displacement of the CH3 domains after fitting them jointly to the WT reference. Each panel is a system and each line is a replicate. Stored time includes equilibration; the primary samples span 3.16–10.11 ns at 50 ps intervals.
figures.interpretation: Inspect late drift and replicate disagreement before interpreting the corresponding mean. Compare this panel with the window-sensitivity figure.
figures.limitation: Visual stability does not prove equilibration or convergence. Short-lived events between sampled frames can be missed.

figures.title: Contact-count sensitivity to cutoffs and windows
figures.question: Do total interface differences retain their direction when cutoffs or start frames change?
figures.reading: Rows separate heavy-atom contacts and salt-bridge candidates. Left panels vary cutoff at the primary window; right panels vary start frame at the primary cutoff. All use 50 ps samples. Lines identify variants relative to WT.
figures.interpretation: Changes across cutoffs indicate definition dependence; changes across start times indicate temporal dependence.
figures.limitation: These are nested subsets of the same three trajectories per system, not additional independent replicates. Sensitivity checks are descriptive and do not prove convergence, equivalence, or a causal mechanism.

figures.title: 10 ps versus 50 ps occupancy comparisons
figures.question: Does the coarser primary sampling change residue-pair occupancy differences?
figures.reading: Each point is a variant/residue-pair comparison. The diagonal indicates agreement between cadences. Panel titles give the largest absolute deviation, in percentage points.
figures.interpretation: Points close to the diagonal support the primary sampling for occupancy, but do not establish contact lifetimes.
figures.limitation: These are nested subsets of the same three trajectories per system, not additional independent replicates. Sensitivity checks are descriptive and do not prove convergence, equivalence, or a causal mechanism.

figures.title: Largest primary contact changes across analysis choices
figures.question: Which highlighted findings persist across the full cutoff/window/cadence grid?
figures.reading: Rows were selected by largest primary changes, not by sensitivity performance. Each row uses its interaction-specific cutoffs. Column labels are start frame / stride / cutoff index. Red and blue retain the same meaning as the primary heatmaps.
figures.interpretation: A stable sign is evidence of directional consistency across these settings; the CSV gives minimum and maximum effects.
figures.limitation: These are nested subsets of the same three trajectories per system, not additional independent replicates. Sensitivity checks are descriptive and do not prove convergence, equivalence, or a causal mechanism.

figures.title: MM/GBSA sensitivity to the start of the window
figures.question: Does the mean energetic ordering depend on how much early production is excluded?
figures.reading: Each colored line uses a different start frame with the same ending frame and existing 50 ps energy snapshots. Positive values indicate less favorable energy than WT.
figures.interpretation: Check whether effects retain their sign and how much their magnitude changes. No new energy calculations are performed.
figures.limitation: These are nested subsets of the same three trajectories per system, not additional independent replicates. Sensitivity checks are descriptive and do not prove convergence, equivalence, or a causal mechanism.

figures.title: Structural sensitivity to the start of the window
figures.question: Do structural mean differences change in later subsets of the trajectories?
figures.reading: Each panel is a structural observable; lines identify starting frames and show variant minus WT means at 50 ps sampling.
figures.interpretation: Substantial movement across windows means a single full-window average is incomplete.
figures.limitation: These are nested subsets of the same three trajectories per system, not additional independent replicates. Sensitivity checks are descriptive and do not prove convergence, equivalence, or a causal mechanism.

sensitivity_summary: Heavy-atom occupancy differences: the largest 10 ps versus 50 ps deviation is 6.90 percentage points.
Salt-bridge candidate occupancy differences: the largest 10 ps versus 50 ps deviation is 2.05 percentage points.
D265A mean MM/GBSA difference from WT ranges from +8.16 to +10.02 kcal/mol across start frames.
S298A mean MM/GBSA difference from WT ranges from -1.62 to -0.51 kcal/mol across start frames.
A327S mean MM/GBSA difference from WT ranges from -3.80 to -2.41 kcal/mol across start frames.
15 of 15 highlighted primary variant/pair changes retain direction across all 18 settings per interaction type. This is a descriptive sign check, not a significance test.
